# @lidtop/opencode-sessions

Find the conversation, not just the project. Search recorded OpenCode sessions across projects, including message text, and get back to the one you need. The sidebar keeps every active agent in view, across projects.

![Sessions browser searching for cache discussions across projects with a selected message preview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZackarySantana/opcode/main/docs/images/sessions-browser.png)

## Install

Requires OpenCode **2.2.0 or newer in the 2.x line**.

```sh
opencode plugin add @lidtop/opencode-sessions
```

Or add it to `plugins` in your global `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc` (or `opencode.json`), keeping your existing entries:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": ["@lidtop/opencode-sessions"]
}
```

**Where it runs.** Install it globally so opened projects keep their index up to date even without the browser open. The server builds and owns the index and the Agents list; the terminal's browser and sidebar read them over plugin RPC. A client-only install in `cli.json` does not work, because both need the server plugin.

## Use

Run `/sessions` or select **All sessions** in the command palette to open the browser dialog. `/sessions-all` and `/all-sessions` are aliases: names already used by other commands are left alone, and the first free name becomes the primary command. The palette entry works even if every name is taken.

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `↑` / `↓`, `j` / `k` | Move selection |
| `/` | Type in the search box: a case-insensitive JavaScript regular expression, applied as you type |
| `p` | Filter by project, including all of its indexed directories; clears the search |
| `s` | Show or hide child sessions (hidden initially) |
| `enter` | Close the dialog and open the selected session |
| `x` | Clear the search and project filter; keep child visibility |
| `r` | Resynchronize changed sessions and message history |
| `esc` | Undo one step: stop typing, clear the search, drop the project filter, then close |

Search matches titles, full directory paths, and complete indexed user and assistant messages, each separately, so anchors such as `^/home` apply to a whole field. Results are newest-updated first. Filters and matching apply **before** the newest 200 matches are kept; refine the search or project filter for older ones. Opening the browser resets its filters.

Expressions use Unicode mode when valid, otherwise legacy syntax, and are limited to 256 characters. Invalid expressions stay editable. Matching runs in a background worker with a three-second budget; when it expires, the matches found so far are shown, marked **partial**. The browser re-queries every five seconds while open.

When the dialog is wide enough, the preview shows the newest matching message centered on the match (up to 4,096 characters), the latest model, model count, indexed message count, recorded cost, and token counters. These are **indexed historical totals**, not current context use or billing totals.

`enter` opens the session in this terminal, whichever directory it belongs to.

## Active sessions

The **Agents** section at the top of the sidebar lists root sessions from every project and location that need attention, numbered in the order they became active. The server keeps the list, so every terminal connected to it shows the same rows in the same order. The order doesn't change as their states do:

| Mark | State | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `●` | needs you | A permission or question is waiting anywhere in the session or its subagents, or a retry needs you to act |
| `✗` | failed | The run failed, and you haven't opened the session since, or did so within the last 10 minutes |
| `✓` | finished | The run finished, and you haven't opened the session since, or did so within the last 10 minutes |
| `↻` | retrying | The session or a subagent is retrying after an error |
| `○` | working | The session or a subagent is running |

Subagents are rolled up into their root session ("2 agents"); only the root needs to be seen for a finished run to drop out, in every terminal, and archived sessions never appear. A run you've seen stays listed, its mark muted, for `inbox.keepRead` minutes after you first open the session following its finish, in any terminal, however long ago it finished. Opening it again doesn't extend that, and a run that finishes while you watch counts as seen then. The session you are in isn't listed in that terminal. Each row shows its project, the time since it finished or was last active, and its title. Five rows are shown; "+N more" opens the full list. With no active sessions and no way back, the section is hidden.

- Click a row, or run `/go <n>`, to open session n. `/go` alone, or **Go to active session** in the command palette, lists them all.
- After the plugin takes you somewhere (a sidebar click, `/go`, the list, or opening a session from `/sessions`), a **Back to …** row appears above the list; click it, or run `/back`, `/previous`, or `/go back`. Going back again retraces each step. Switching sessions any other way, such as with tabs or going home, forgets the trail.
- `/go`, `/back`, and `/previous` are each skipped when another command already uses that name; the palette entries (**Go to active session**, **Go back**) always work.

The server plugin reads the newest 100 root sessions when it starts and follows the server's live events; terminals read the whole list again whenever they reconnect. A server plugin can't read which sessions are running or what they ask, so after starting, or whenever it may have missed events, it asks a connected terminal to read that once; until one does, a run that started earlier may be missing. OpenCode records only that a run was seen, not when, so the server knows when a run was seen only if the plugin was running at the time; it keeps those times in memory, not across a server restart. A finished session outside the newest 100 root sessions appears only once it becomes active again.

Alerts (`inbox.notify`), the back trail, and leaving out the session you're in stay with each terminal: every terminal alerts once for each new request or finish the server announces, except in the session family it's on.

### From other plugins

To open a session so that **Back to …** returns to where the user was, dispatch `opcode-sessions.navigate` with the session ID instead of navigating directly:

```ts
api.keymap.dispatch("opcode-sessions.navigate", sessionID)
```

It works from any input mode, including over a dialog, but only navigates: close your own dialog first (`api.ui.dialog.clear()`). With `inbox.enabled: false` it still navigates, without a back trail.

## Indexing

The server indexes each loaded location and follows session lifecycle, usage, content-update, and revert events, even without a terminal open.

- **Resilient refresh:** live subscriptions reconnect and reconcile immediately. A session that changes while being read is retried once idle, and individual failures retry up to three times without delaying other sessions. One busy or failing session never stops a refresh; deletions are still reconciled, and busy or failed counts are reported. Unchanged sessions are skipped, and overlapping refreshes are coalesced. Existing results stay searchable during slow resynchronization.
- **Full history:** server context holds only the active post-compaction window. To make earlier text searchable, the terminal fetches **full message history** in the background the first time the browser opens in each terminal process and on `r`, and uploads it in bounded, validated batches (at most 32 messages, 1 MiB of text per message, and 2 MiB per batch). Oversized messages are left out and counted, never truncated. Sessions that change or are deleted mid-upload are skipped and picked up by a later pass.
- **What's indexed:** only user and assistant text, not reasoning, tool inputs or results, attachments, or system and synthetic messages. Compaction never removes indexed text; reverts do. Deleted sessions and their descendants are removed and guarded against late writes, including after restarts. Forks sharing message IDs stay separate.

## Options

Set these on the **server** (`opencode.jsonc`); they apply to every terminal:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": [
    { "package": "@lidtop/opencode-sessions", "options": { "database": "/absolute/server/path/sessions.sqlite", "inbox": { "keepRead": 5 } } }
  ]
}
```

- `database`: where the index is stored. Relative paths resolve from the server's OpenCode state directory; the terminal ignores this option and uses RPC. `:memory:` is useful for tests, not durable history. The default is `$XDG_STATE_HOME/opencode/opencode-sessions-all/sessions.sqlite` (or `~/.local/state/opencode/opencode-sessions-all/sessions.sqlite`).
- `inbox.keepRead` (default `10`): whole minutes a finished or failed run stays listed after you've seen it; `0` removes it as soon as you open it.

Configure the rest of the active-sessions sidebar on the **terminal**: terminal extensions receive options only from global `~/.config/opencode/cli.json`. Keep the server entry too; the terminal loads the plugin once, with these options.

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/v2/cli.json",
  "plugins": [
    { "package": "@lidtop/opencode-sessions", "options": { "inbox": { "rows": 8, "notify": true } } }
  ]
}
```

- `inbox.enabled` (default `true`): `false` removes the sidebar section and its commands (`/go`, `/back`, `/previous`) from this terminal, which then stops following the list. The server keeps it for other terminals.
- `inbox.rows` (default `5`): rows shown before "+N more".
- `inbox.notify` (default `false`): a desktop notification and sound while the terminal is unfocused, plus a toast, for each new permission or question and each finished or failed run, except in the session family you are in. They follow your OpenCode attention settings.

## Data and privacy

**The database contains raw user and assistant text**, session titles, filesystem paths, model IDs, and usage metrics. Text can include secrets, pasted file contents, or sensitive material repeated by the model, even though tool payloads and attachments are excluded. The index is not encrypted, and it is a cache, not a transcript backup.

**Only the server opens SQLite.** New database files use `0600` and new directories `0700` on Unix filesystems; existing permissions are not changed, so check legacy or custom files and their WAL/SHM sidecars. Every authenticated client of the server can search its index; there is no per-project access boundary. SQLite `secure_delete` overwrites deleted text in the database file, but this is not secure erasure of WAL frames, copies, or backups.

## Replacing opencode-sessions-all

The default database path is the same as `opencode-sessions-all`'s, and its `sessions`, `messages`, and `backfill` tables are kept; older indexes gain additive columns and `opcode_sessions_*` tables, with no destructive conversion, so older processes sharing the file keep working. Back up the database first, then **remove `opencode-sessions-all`** rather than running both writers against the same file.

## Development

From the repository root:

```sh
mise exec -- bun test plugins/sessions/test
mise exec -- bun run typecheck
mise run dev sessions
```

The build bundles the private `@opcode/core`, `@opcode/tabs`, and `@opcode/ui` workspaces into the package; OpenCode, OpenTUI, and Solid stay external. The real-host RPC test needs an OpenCode binary on `PATH` or at `~/.opencode/bin/opencode`, and reports loudly when it is skipped.

# @lidtop/opencode-sessions

## 0.4.0

### Minor Changes

- 62c9603: Require OpenCode 2.2.0 and OpenTUI 0.7.

## 0.3.2

### Patch Changes

- 5ccffe8: Shared code moved into helpers every plugin bundles: the refresh schedule now also works outside the terminal, and there are new helpers for state shared by a server's projects, RPC contracts and handlers, and following a server's state. For Context, Feed, Later, and Media nothing changes. In Cost, Review, Snippets, and Sessions, a call the terminal aborted is no longer reported as a failure. In Sessions, every project open on a server now shares one search index connection and one writer per database file, rather than possibly one per project.
- 1321e5b: The Agents sidebar now comes from the OpenCode server, so every terminal connected to it lists the same sessions, in the same order, with the same states, and a finish you've seen in one terminal counts as seen in all of them. Each terminal still leaves out the session it's on, keeps its own back trail, and alerts once per new request or finish when `inbox.notify` is on. `inbox.keepRead` is now a server option (`opencode.json(c)`, not `cli.json`); `inbox.rows`, `inbox.notify`, and `inbox.enabled` stay terminal options. The sidebar needs the server plugin, as the browser already did. The time a run was first seen is known only if the server plugin was running then, and is not kept across a server restart.
- e91635a: Shared code that Feed and GH PR Status use moved into helpers every plugin bundles: the minute clock that ages views, and sending changes to the server in order while showing them at once. Nothing changes for any plugin.

## 0.3.1

### Patch Changes

- abc551c: Finished and failed sessions stay in the Agents sidebar for 10 minutes after you first open them, with a muted mark, instead of dropping out right away. They keep their place and their number for `/go` while listed. Set `inbox.keepRead` in `cli.json` to a different number of minutes, or `0` to drop them as soon as you open them.
- abc551c: The Agents sidebar no longer freezes when its event stream silently stops delivering, which left finished sessions listed as working, missed new ones, and kept sessions you had opened. Like OpenCode itself, it now reconnects after 45 seconds without even a keepalive and reloads the list.

## 0.3.0

### Minor Changes

- f5d0ff2: Add an Agents section at the top of the sidebar listing active sessions across all projects: working, retrying, waiting on you, or finished or failed since you last looked, with subagents rolled up into their session. Rows keep the order they became active; click one or run `/go <n>` to open it, and `/go back` (or the Back row) to return. Optional notifications for new requests and finished runs are off by default; configure everything under `inbox` in `cli.json`. `/sessions` now opens sessions from other directories directly instead of copying a resume command.
- a5ede26: `/sessions` opens as an extra-large dialog with more room for titles and a wider preview. `/back` and `/previous` return along the back trail, like the sidebar's **Back to …** row. Other plugins can dispatch `opcode-sessions.navigate` with a session ID to open it while recording the back trail.

### Patch Changes

- bb097fd: Require OpenCode 2.1.3 or newer.
- fe9d281: Remove the `/opcode-sessions` and `/opcode-go` slash names. Use `/sessions`, `/sessions-all`, or `/all-sessions` to browse sessions, and `/go` for active sessions. When `/go` belongs to another command, use **Go to active session** in the command palette.
- 14bdfde: The Agents sidebar, `/go`, and its list no longer include the session you're in.
- 2549f8e: Hide the Agents sidebar section while there are no active sessions and no way back.
- e7e3fcb: `/sessions` opens as a large centered dialog, like `/feed` and `/ghpr`, instead of a full-screen page. The search box filters as you type, `p` picks a project in place, and `esc` steps back one filter at a time before closing.
- 1708674: Move Later's prompt paste helper into the shared UI package so Snippets can reuse it. No behavior changes.
- 44bad65: The Pull requests and Feeds sidebar sections show their refresh countdown beside the title instead of on a line of their own. Those sections and Agents no longer add a line saying there's nothing to show; they show just the title.
- e85fab8: The shared tabbed dialog can keep its open tab when shown again, for Later. No behavior changes.
- f27f920: The shared item card can lead with its title when an item has no head, for Later. No behavior changes.

## 0.2.3

### Patch Changes

- 439c23e: Tag the package with the `opencode` and `opencode-plugin` npm keywords so plugin directories such as OpenDock can list it.

## 0.2.2

### Patch Changes

- a8e520d: Standardize the package READMEs: install with `opencode plugin add` first, show screenshots, and use the same sections and wording across every plugin.

## 0.2.1

### Patch Changes

- e6b5093: Context no longer lets missing, negative, or non-finite provider usage values corrupt its token totals. History pagination, live-event reconnection, and usage normalization now behave consistently across plugins, and Cost always closes its ledger on unload. Errors with an empty message now show a readable fallback instead of a blank notification.
- 6eaeb52: Context and Cost now share one coalesced refresh from the bundled core utilities. Cost dashboard reads time out after 30 seconds instead of blocking later refreshes, and refresh-failure warnings in both stay visible until a retry succeeds. Later and Sessions only rebuild against the updated shared core.
- 1ae9d93: Create new Cost and Later databases owner-only (0600 files in a 0700 directory) before SQLite writes to them, as Sessions already did; existing database permissions are left unchanged. All plugins now share one XDG state-path resolver.
- e70e939: Measure and truncate labels with the host renderer's width method in every plugin, so Cost project, model, and warning labels no longer overflow with wide characters such as CJK or emoji. Cost, Later, and Sessions keyboard hints with a matching command are now clickable, and all views take their colors from the shared theme palette.
- ea7786e: Keep history import working when the TUI and server run different Sessions versions, and stop dropping the legacy per-message revision table so older processes sharing the index keep writing.
- 613bcf8: Make session indexing resilient. A busy or failing session no longer aborts a refresh or skips deletion reconciliation; busy sessions are retried quietly once idle, and counts are reported. History import skips deleted or changed sessions and leaves out (and counts) messages over 1 MiB instead of stopping. Unchanged sessions are skipped on refresh and history import, overlapping refreshes are coalesced, and history now synchronizes the first time the browser opens rather than on every TUI launch. Reverted messages are removed from the index while compacted history stays searchable. Index writes use immediate SQLite transactions, so a second writer cannot abort them; descendants of deleted sessions stay deleted; and tombstones no longer hide a session the server later returns. The index enables SQLite `secure_delete`.
- 613bcf8: Improve search. Expensive expressions return the matches found before the time budget, marked partial, instead of failing. Searches no longer wait behind index writes and reuse one regex worker. Titles, directories, and messages are matched separately so anchors such as `^/home` work, Unicode mode is used when the expression allows it, and the 256-character limit counts characters. Previews center on the match without splitting graphemes. Enter now opens the selected session while results refresh in the background.

## 0.2.0

### Minor Changes

- 805bb55: Publish independently versioned OpenCode V2 plugins with bundled private helpers and terminal extensions.

### Patch Changes

- 8f1a01b: Balance theme colors: use normal foreground for page/dialog titles and shortcut keys, muted labels and neutral borders, accent hues for sections/charts, and interactive hues for values. Preserve the theme's contrasting selection foreground/background pair.
